Continuation facts for the streetcar turning and lane pages followed by confusable pairs, each tied to one manual page; knowledge-graph hints (group, difficulty, confusable pair) sit only in the trailing Why it matters line of each block.

FACT_ID: sec07-R01 | anchor: A07
Never turn across the path of a streetcar or train moving your way in the next lane, even while it is stopped. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars; continuation; difficulty hard.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R02 | anchor: A07
Do not turn in front of an approaching streetcar or light rail train unless it is safe, and slow down and look both ways before crossing tracks at an intersection. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R03 | anchor: A07
When turning across tracks, look both ways for streetcars, signal, and where a left turn signal is present, wait for that signal before turning left over the tracks. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R04 | anchor: A07
Watch for riders near streetcar and train stops, since passengers may dash across lanes to catch one, and follow pedestrian signals so people can cross safely. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars and pedestrians; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R05 | anchor: A07
Check for streetcars and trains before changing lanes, since one may be close behind you, and avoid sudden braking or surprise moves around them because they cannot stop quickly. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars; continuation; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R06 | anchor: A07
If your vehicle touches a streetcar or train, wait for the operator or the police to tell you what to do. [A07]
Why it matters: group streetcars; continuation; difficulty easy.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0074]

FACT_ID: sec07-R07 | anchor: A01
For an emergency vehicle you pull right and stay stopped until it passes or an officer waves you on, while for a police stop you also turn off the engine and keep your hands on the wheel. [A01]
Why it matters: group emergency and police; confusable emergency vehicle yield versus police stop; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R08 | anchor: A01
Pulling over for an emergency vehicle, avoid stopping in an intersection; pulling over for police, also avoid stopping in an intersection or on a highway center median. [A01]
Why it matters: group emergency and police; confusable intersection rule versus median rule; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0066]

FACT_ID: sec07-R09 | anchor: A02
A work zone with no workers in sight still carries its temporary speed limit, so an empty work zone is no reason to speed back up before the end sign. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; confusable workers present versus workers absent; difficulty hard.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R10 | anchor: A02
At an automated flagger, red light with the arm down means stop, and flashing yellow with the arm up means go; it is not a green light signal. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; confusable red and arm down versus yellow and arm up; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R11 | anchor: A02
Flaggers and automated flagger devices are what you meet on two-lane road work zones, while on freeways you usually keep moving through narrowed or shifted lanes. [A02]
Why it matters: group work zones; confusable two-lane work zone versus freeway work zone; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0067]

FACT_ID: sec07-R12 | anchor: A04
A railroad advance sign only warns that a crossing is ahead, while the crossbuck assembly at the crossing carries a yield or stop sign that you must obey. [A04]
Why it matters: group railroad signs; confusable advance warning versus crossbuck; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec07-R13 | anchor: A05
A posted stop sign at a crossing means you stop even with no train in sight, while flashing red lights, a visible close train or a flagger signal are the other triggers to stop. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad stops; confusable stop sign versus active warnings; difficulty hard.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec07-R14 | anchor: A05
If you are stuck on the tracks, getting out and away comes before notifying the railroad at the ENS sign, and notifying is done only if it is safe. [A05]
Why it matters: group railroad emergencies; confusable escape first versus notify first; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0072]

FACT_ID: sec07-R15 | anchor: A06
A stopped streetcar loading passengers is a reason to stay behind it, not to pass, until it moves again or the riders are safely away. [A06]
Why it matters: group streetcars; confusable stopped streetcar versus stopped car; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0073]
